concept.title: The Anti-Fibonacci Sequence: Numbers That Avoid the Golden Ratio at All Costs
concept.concept_description: The Fibonacci sequence is defined by F(n+1) = F(n) + F(n-1) and converges to the golden ratio. Define the ANTI-Fibonacci sequence: A(n+1) is the smallest positive integer that is NOT equal to A(n) + A(n-1). The sequence begins 1, 1, 2, 4, 7, 11, 16, ... (each term avoids being the sum of the two previous terms). Conjecture: The anti-Fibonacci sequence A(n) grows as A(n) ~ n^2/4, and the ratio A(n)/n^2 converges to 1/4. More precisely, A(n) = floor(n^2/4) + O(1). The sequence avoids the golden ratio entirely — the ratio A(n+1)/A(n) does NOT converge, instead oscillating between 1 and 2. The complement of the anti-Fibonacci sequence (numbers that ARE sums of two previous anti-Fibonacci numbers) has density 0. Test: compute A(n) for n up to 10^6 and verify A(n)/n^2 approaches 1/4. Prove A(n) = floor(n^2/4) + O(1) by induction. Impact: a beautiful counterpoint to the Fibonacci sequence — instead of converging to a constant, it grows quadratically while systematically avoiding addition.

import Mathlib

/-! # Writhe as a well-defined braid invariant for cognitive equivalence

We model a *cognitive process* as a finite word over the Artin generators `σ_i`
of the braid group `B_n`.  Each generator `σ_i` contributes `+1` to the *writhe*
and each inverse `σ_i⁻¹` contributes `-1`.  The writhe of a word is the sum of
these signed contributions.

The main results are:

* `writheWord_append` — writhe is additive under concatenation of processes;
* `writheWord_comm_rel` — writhe is invariant under the far-commutation braid
  relation `σ_i σ_j = σ_j σ_i` (`|i - j| > 1`);
* `writheWord_braid_rel` — writhe is invariant under the Yang–Baxter braid
  relation `σ_i σ_{i+1} σ_i = σ_{i+1} σ_i σ_{i+1}`;
* `writhe` — the induced group homomorphism `BraidGroup →* Multiplicative ℤ`,
  obtained by descending the free-group writhe through the braid relations.  Its
  existence is precisely the statement that the writhe is a *well-defined braid
  invariant*: it depends only on the class of a process modulo braid
  equivalence, with no circular dependence on a chosen word representative.
-/

namespace CognitiveBraid

/-! ## Word-level model

A signed generator is a pair `(i, s)` where `i : ℕ` is the Artin index and
`s : Bool` is the sign (`true` for `σ_i`, `false` for `σ_i⁻¹`).  A cognitive
process is a finite list of signed generators. -/

/-- A signed Artin generator: index and sign (`true = σ_i`, `false = σ_i⁻¹`). -/
abbrev SignedGen : Type := ℕ × Bool

/-- Signed contribution of a single generator to the writhe. -/
def sign (g : SignedGen) : ℤ := if g.2 then 1 else -1

/-- The writhe of a cognitive process (word): the sum of signed contributions. -/
def writheWord (w : List SignedGen) : ℤ := (w.map sign).sum

@[simp] theorem writheWord_nil : writheWord [] = 0 := rfl

@[simp] theorem writheWord_cons (g : SignedGen) (w : List SignedGen) :
    writheWord (g :: w) = sign g + writheWord w := by
  simp [writheWord]

/-- Writhe is additive under concatenation of processes. -/
theorem writheWord_append (u v : List SignedGen) :
    writheWord (u ++ v) = writheWord u + writheWord v := by
  simp [writheWord]

/-- **Far-commutation invariance.**  Swapping two adjacent generators (as in the
relation `σ_i σ_j = σ_j σ_i` for `|i - j| > 1`) leaves the writhe unchanged, in
any context `a … b` and for any signs. -/
theorem writheWord_comm_rel (a b : List SignedGen) (i j : ℕ) (s t : Bool) :
    writheWord (a ++ (i, s) :: (j, t) :: b) =
      writheWord (a ++ (j, t) :: (i, s) :: b) := by
  simp [writheWord_append]
  ring

/-- **Braid (Yang–Baxter) invariance.**  Replacing `σ_i σ_{i+1} σ_i` by
`σ_{i+1} σ_i σ_{i+1}` leaves the writhe unchanged, in any context and for any
signs. -/
theorem writheWord_braid_rel (a b : List SignedGen) (i : ℕ) (s t u : Bool) :
    writheWord (a ++ (i, s) :: (i + 1, t) :: (i, u) :: b) =
      writheWord (a ++ (i + 1, t) :: (i, s) :: (i + 1, u) :: b) := by
  simp only [writheWord_append, writheWord_cons, sign]
  ring

/-! ## Group-theoretic invariant

We now realise the writhe as an honest group homomorphism out of the braid
group, showing it descends through the defining relations. -/

/-- Indices `i` and `j` are far apart when `|i - j| > 1`. -/
def FarApart (i j : ℕ) : Prop := i + 1 < j ∨ j + 1 < i

/-- The set of braid relators inside the free group on Artin generators:
the far-commutation relators `σ_i σ_j σ_i⁻¹ σ_j⁻¹` for `|i - j| > 1`, together
with the Yang–Baxter relators `σ_i σ_{i+1} σ_i σ_{i+1}⁻¹ σ_i⁻¹ σ_{i+1}⁻¹`. -/

      {FreeGroup.of i * FreeGroup.of j * (FreeGroup.of i)⁻¹ * (FreeGroup.of j)⁻¹})
  ∪ (⋃ (i : ℕ),
      {FreeGroup.of i * FreeGroup.of (i + 1) * FreeGroup.of i

abbrev BraidGroup : Type := PresentedGroup braidRels

`+1` (written multiplicatively in `Multiplicative ℤ`). -/
def writheFree : FreeGroup ℕ →* Multiplicative ℤ :=
  FreeGroup.lift (fun _ => Multiplicative.ofAdd (1 : ℤ))

    writheFree (FreeGroup.of i) = Multiplicative.ofAdd (1 : ℤ) := by
  simp [writheFree]

uses each generator equally often with `+` and `-` signs. -/
theorem writheFree_relators (r : FreeGroup ℕ) (hr : r ∈ braidRels) :
    writheFree r = 1 := by
  rcases hr with hr | hr
  · simp only [Set.mem_iUnion, Set.mem_singleton_iff] at hr
    obtain ⟨i, j, -, rfl⟩ := hr
    simp only [map_mul, map_inv, writheFree_of]
    group
  · simp only [Set.mem_iUnion, Set.mem_singleton_iff] at hr
    obtain ⟨i, rfl⟩ := hr
    simp only [map_mul, map_inv, writheFree_of]
    group

writhe kills every braid relator, it descends to a group homomorphism on the
braid group.  This is exactly the statement that the writhe of a cognitive
process depends only on its braid-equivalence class. -/
def writhe : BraidGroup →* Multiplicative ℤ :=
  PresentedGroup.toGroup (f := fun _ => Multiplicative.ofAdd (1 : ℤ)) writheFree_relators

/-- The descended invariant sends each Artin generator to `+1`. -/
@[simp] theorem writhe_of (i : ℕ) :
    writhe (PresentedGroup.of i) = Multiplicative.ofAdd (1 : ℤ) := by
  simp [writhe, PresentedGroup.toGroup.of]

# Future Directions — Knots That Think

Five self-contained, falsifiable conjectures arising from this cycle's finding
that, among the trivial, trefoil, and figure-eight "thought-knots", only the
trefoil carries positive quantum-dimension information (`½ log 3`), while the
"confused" figure-eight is indistinguishable from thinking nothing.

## 1. The Golden Thought: creative capacity grows at rate `log φ`

Model a train of thought as a sequence of braiding moves on a chain of Fibonacci
anyons, whose fusion spaces have dimensions equal to consecutive Fibonacci
numbers. The creative capacity of an `n`-step thought is the logarithm of its
fusion-space dimension, which should equal `n · log φ` for the golden ratio
`φ = (1+√5)/2`, with the space itself of dimension `F_{n+1}`.

**The key insight is** that a thought's capacity is not a fixed number but an
*exponential resource* whose growth rate is a single universal constant, the
golden ratio, distinguishing an unbounded creative sector from the quantized,
bounded `√3` sector seen in the trefoil.

**Why now?** The exact `½ log 3` value for the trefoil shows the quantum-dimension
measure is sharp and computable; extending from a single knot to a growing
anyonic chain is the natural next scale, and the Fibonacci recurrence makes the
growth rate exactly pinnable rather than merely estimated.

## 2. Double-cover homology decides which thoughts are visible

For a knot `K`, the modulus of its Jones polynomial at `e^{iπ/3}` equals
`(√3)^d`, where `d` is the number of independent `Z/3` cycles in the double
branched cover of `K`. Conjecture: across the twist-knot and two-bridge families,
a thought carries positive information exactly when `d > 0`, and this can be read
off from a single congruence on the knot's determinant.

**The key insight is** that "does this thought carry information?" is not
topologically mysterious — it is governed entirely by three-torsion in a single
homology group, reducing a hard invariant to an arithmetic congruence.

**Why now?** The figure-eight's surprising collapse to zero information is exactly
the `d = 0` case; recognizing this pattern turns an isolated anomaly into a
predictive, testable classification across an infinite family.

## 3. Writhe is not enough: a two-invariant cost bound

Net topological charge (writhe) forces a tight lower bound on the number of
firing events realizing a thought, but it is blind to how strands interleave.
Introduce a second measure — the minimal number of adjacent swaps needed to
achieve the thought's permutation of brain regions — and conjecture that the true
firing cost is at least the maximum of the two, with explicit families where each
term dominates.

**The key insight is** that cognitive cost has two irreducible sources, an
abelian one (net directed charge) and a non-abelian one (reconfiguration of
regions), and neither alone captures the difficulty of a thought.

**Why now?** The writhe bound is already sharp for the trefoil; its very sharpness
exposes that it says nothing about permutation complexity, motivating the second,
orthogonal invariant precisely where the first saturates.

## 4. Compound thoughts add their information

When two thoughts are joined end-to-end (a connected sum of their knots), their
quantum-dimension information should add exactly: a compound of `k` independent
creative insights carries `k · ½ log 3`, and gluing on a trivial thought changes
nothing.

**The key insight is** that the information of a thought is an *extensive*
quantity — it scales linearly with the number of independent insights it
contains, so creativity accumulates additively rather than saturating.

**Why now?** Having a clean closed value for a single creative insight makes the
additivity law directly checkable, and it predicts a linear ladder of information
levels that can be compared against graded notions of thought complexity.

## 5. A cyclotomic spectrum separates thoughts

Instead of one evaluation point, record the whole vector of Jones moduli at
primitive `p`-th roots of unity for small primes `p`. Conjecture that the trivial
thought is the unique one with an all-ones spectrum, that trefoil and
figure-eight are separated by this spectrum even though they coincide in the
`e^{iπ/3}` coordinate, and that a small, explicit set of primes suffices to tell
apart all thoughts below a fixed complexity.

**The key insight is** that a single number cannot classify thoughts — the
figure-eight proves this by mimicking triviality at one point — but a short
spectrum of cyclotomic evaluations restores full discriminating power.

**Why now?** This cycle produced an explicit collision (figure-eight vs. trivial
at one root of unity); the natural remedy is to widen the probe from one root to a
spectrum, and the small crossing-number knot tables make the separation claim
immediately falsifiable.
